name: Conversational Settings
description: Lets users edit module settings via natural language — TPM parses the request, identifies the target setting, and either proposes the change or applies it directly via the settings-write verb, gated by Application Mode and the Enable Settings Write master switch. Phase 1: scalar settings only.

enableDetection.label: Enable Detection
enableDetection.description: Master switch for natural-language settings detection. When on, TPM watches user turns for phrases that match settings-edit intent. When off, the user must edit settings directly via the Modules tab. On is the typical default for ergonomics.

triggerPhrases.label: Trigger Phrases
triggerPhrases.description: Comma-separated list of substring patterns that suggest a settings-edit intent. Matched case-insensitively. Tune for false-positive avoidance — phrases like set and change are broad and may trigger on non-settings contexts; the fuzzy-match step downstream usually filters those out.
triggerPhrases.default: turn on, turn off, enable, disable, set, change, raise, lower, switch, flip, toggle, update setting, configure

applicationMode.label: Application Mode
applicationMode.description: How TPM responds to a recognized settings-edit intent. propose surfaces the exact panel edit needed (e.g., Modules tab → Database Access → toggle off) for the user to apply manually. apply attempts to apply the change directly via the settings-write verb — falls back to propose if Enable Settings Write is off or the host refuses the write for any reason (undeclared key, bad value, autonomous mode active, kv-table target, host-managed value). ask prompts the user to choose per occurrence. Default propose is the conservative choice: flip to apply only once you also want the write gate itself on (see Enable Settings Write below) — the two settings are independent switches, and this one alone never writes anything.

enableSettingsWrite.label: Enable Settings Write
enableSettingsWrite.description: The master gate the host enforces on every settings write this module attempts. While this is off — and off is the default — set-module-setting is refused outright for every request regardless of Application Mode, however the operator phrases it. Turning it on does not by itself cause any write: Application Mode must also be apply (or ask, with the operator choosing apply) for a write to be attempted at all, and every write is still subject to the host's other checks (schema membership, value validation, the self-reference denylist protecting this module's own settings, and the bar on writing during mode.ticket-pr or War Mode). This setting and Application Mode are two independent switches; neither one opens the other.

requireConfirmationFor.label: Require Confirmation For
requireConfirmationFor.description: Comma-separated list of setting categories that require explicit user confirmation before TPM proposes or applies a change. all is a sentinel that means everything; the other tags (secrets, allowlists, modes) name categories TPM recognizes per the configured manifests. Tighten this list to skip confirmation on routine settings; widen to add safety friction.

fuzzyMatchThreshold.label: Fuzzy Match Threshold
fuzzyMatchThreshold.description: Percent confidence required for TPM to act on a fuzzy-matched setting name. Default 70 is conservative; raise to 85 for strict matching (fewer false positives, more I'm not sure what setting you mean prompts); lower to 50 for permissive matching (more direct action, more risk of acting on the wrong setting).
